title: Psalms Chapter 128 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 128 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 128 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 128.

questions.question: According to Psalms 128:1, who is considered blessed?
options: Every one that feareth the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Every one that feareth the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:1 states that blessed is every one that feareth the LORD.

questions.question: What must one do to be blessed according to Psalms 128:1?
questions.correctAnswer: Walk in his ways
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:1 mentions that blessed is the one who feareth the LORD and walketh in his ways.

questions.question: According to Psalms 128:2, what will you eat?
questions.correctAnswer: The labour of thine hands
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:2 says, 'For thou shalt eat the labour of thine hands.'

questions.question: How does Psalms 128:2 describe the happiness of the blessed person?
options: Happy shalt thou be, and it shall be well with thee
Happy shalt thou be, and rich in gold
Happy shalt thou be, and famous in the land
Happy shalt thou be, and strong in battle
questions.correctAnswer: Happy shalt thou be, and it shall be well with thee
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:2 states that the blessed person will be happy and it shall be well with them.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 128:3 says the wife is like a fruitful olive tree.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:3 says the wife shall be as a fruitful vine, not an olive tree.

questions.question: According to Psalms 128:3, children are compared to what?
options: Olive plants round about the table
Vines by the side of the house
questions.correctAnswer: Olive plants round about the table
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:3 compares children to olive plants round about the table.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 128:4 emphasizes the blessing of the man who feareth the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:4 states, 'Behold, that thus shall the man be blessed that feareth the LORD.'

questions.question: Where shall the LORD bless you from, according to Psalms 128:5?
questions.correctAnswer: Out of Zion
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:5 says, 'The LORD shall bless thee out of Zion.'

questions.question: What will you see all the days of your life according to Psalms 128:5?
questions.correctAnswer: The good of Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:5 promises that you shall see the good of Jerusalem all the days of your life.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 128:6 says you shall see your children's children.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:6 clearly states, 'Yea, thou shalt see thy children's children.'

questions.question: What is upon Israel according to Psalms 128:6?
questions.correctAnswer: Peace
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:6 ends with 'and peace upon Israel.'

questions.question: In Psalms 128, which comes first?
options: Blessed is every one that feareth the LORD
Thy wife shall be as a fruitful vine
The LORD shall bless thee out of Zion
Thou shalt see thy children's children
questions.correctAnswer: Blessed is every one that feareth the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:1 begins with 'Blessed is every one that feareth the LORD,' which comes before the other statements in the chapter.

questions.question: True or False: Psalm 128 mentions eating the labour of others' hands.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:2 says 'thou shalt eat the labour of thine hands,' meaning your own labor, not others'.

questions.question: What is the nature of the song described in Psalms 128:1?
questions.correctAnswer: A song of degrees
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:1 begins with 'A Song of degrees.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 128:3, where is the wife compared to a fruitful vine?
options: By the sides of thine house
questions.correctAnswer: By the sides of thine house
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:3 says, 'Thy wife shall be as a fruitful vine by the sides of thine house.'

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 128 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 128 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 128:3, how is the wife described in relation to the house?
options: As a fruitful vine by the sides of the house
As a strong pillar within the house
As a light shining inside the house
As a river flowing through the house
questions.correctAnswer: As a fruitful vine by the sides of the house
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:3 specifically describes the wife as 'a fruitful vine by the sides of thine house,' symbolizing blessing and nourishment within the family.

questions.question: What does Psalms 128:3 compare children to?
options: Olive plants round about the table
questions.correctAnswer: Olive plants round about the table
questions.explanation: The verse compares children to 'olive plants round about thy table,' indicating growth, strength, and blessing around the family gathering place (Psalms 128:3).

questions.question: What blessing does Psalms 128:4 say will come to the man who fears the LORD?
options: He shall be blessed as described in the previous verse
He will be wealthy beyond measure
questions.correctAnswer: He shall be blessed as described in the previous verse
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:4 refers back to the blessings of a fruitful wife and children like olive plants, affirming that this is the blessing for the man who fears the LORD.

questions.question: How does Psalms 128:3-4 teach about the fruit of fearing the LORD in family life?
options: Fearing the LORD leads to a blessed household with fruitful family relationships
Fearing the LORD guarantees material wealth
Fearing the LORD ensures no hardships in life
Fearing the LORD results in political power
questions.correctAnswer: Fearing the LORD leads to a blessed household with fruitful family relationships
questions.explanation: Verses 3 and 4 show that fearing the LORD brings blessings in the home, including a fruitful wife and flourishing children, emphasizing spiritual fruitfulness in family life.

questions.question: What practical lesson about Christian living can be drawn from the imagery of the fruitful vine and olive plants in Psalms 128:3?
options: Faith and obedience to God lead to growth and blessing in family relationships
Hard work alone guarantees family success
Wealth is the sign of God's favor
Isolation from others is the path to peace
questions.correctAnswer: Faith and obedience to God lead to growth and blessing in family relationships
questions.explanation: The imagery in Psalms 128:3 symbolizes that fearing God and living in His ways fosters a thriving family, reflecting growth and blessing rather than just material success.

questions.question: What does Psalms 128:4 imply about the relationship between fearing the LORD and receiving blessings?
options: Fearing the LORD results in the blessings described in verse 3
Blessings come without any regard to fearing the LORD
Fear of the LORD brings only spiritual blessings but no family blessings
Blessings are guaranteed only through sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: Fearing the LORD results in the blessings described in verse 3
questions.explanation: Verse 4 connects the act of fearing the LORD directly with the blessings of a fruitful wife and children, highlighting the cause and effect relationship.

questions.question: Based on Psalms 128:3-4, what biblical virtue is emphasized for a man to receive blessings on his family?
questions.correctAnswer: Fear of the LORD
questions.explanation: The passage clearly emphasizes that fearing the LORD is the key virtue that results in the blessings described, such as a fruitful wife and flourishing children.

questions.question: What promise does Psalms 128:5 give to those who fear the LORD, complementing the blessings of family life in verses 3 and 4?
options: The LORD shall bless thee out of Zion and you shall see the good of Jerusalem all your life
You will become a great leader among nations
You will never suffer from enemies
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD shall bless thee out of Zion and you shall see the good of Jerusalem all your life
questions.explanation: Verse 5 extends the blessings from family to spiritual and communal blessings from the LORD, promising favor from Zion and the joy of seeing Jerusalem's good.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 128:4, only those who fear the LORD will be blessed as described in verse 3.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 4 states 'Behold, that thus shall the man be blessed that feareth the LORD,' directly linking the blessing to fearing the LORD.

questions.question: What does Psalms 128:6 promise about future generations for those who fear the LORD?
options: They shall see their children's children and peace upon Israel
They shall have wealth for ten generations
They will be rulers over many nations
Their descendants will never face hardship
questions.correctAnswer: They shall see their children's children and peace upon Israel
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:6 specifically promises the blessing of seeing grandchildren and experiencing peace upon Israel, indicating generational blessing and national peace.

questions.question: How does Psalms 128:2 relate to the blessing described in verse 1 about fearing the LORD?
options: Verse 2 promises eating the labor of your hands and happiness if you fear the LORD as instructed in verse 1
Verse 2 talks about wealth unrelated to verse 1
Verse 2 warns of hardships despite fearing the LORD
Verse 2 describes a punishment for disobedience
questions.correctAnswer: Verse 2 promises eating the labor of your hands and happiness if you fear the LORD as instructed in verse 1
questions.explanation: Verse 1 instructs to fear the LORD and walk in His ways, and verse 2 explains the blessing that follows: enjoying the fruit of one's labor and happiness.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 128:5 assures that the LORD's blessing comes from Zion and includes seeing the good of Jerusalem all your life.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 5 clearly states the LORD blesses from Zion and that the faithful shall see the good of Jerusalem throughout their life.

questions.question: If a believer fears the LORD as instructed in Psalms 128:1, what blessing related to daily work is promised in verse 2?
options: They shall eat the labor of their hands and be happy
They will have no need to work
They will receive wealth without effort
questions.correctAnswer: They shall eat the labor of their hands and be happy
questions.explanation: Verse 2 promises that those who fear the LORD will benefit from their own labor and find happiness, showing a connection between obedience and provision.

questions.question: What does Psalms 128:6 say about peace in relation to fearing the LORD and family blessings?
options: Peace will be upon Israel along with seeing grandchildren
Peace is unrelated to fearing the LORD
Peace is guaranteed only in heaven
questions.correctAnswer: Peace will be upon Israel along with seeing grandchildren
questions.explanation: Verse 6 links the blessing of seeing grandchildren with peace upon Israel, indicating that fearing the LORD brings both family and national peace.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 128:1, walking in the LORD's ways is connected with being blessed.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 1 states 'Blessed is every one that feareth the LORD; that walketh in his ways,' connecting obedience and blessing.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 128 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 128.

questions.question: According to Psalms 128:5, from where shall the LORD bless the faithful?
questions.correctAnswer: Zion
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:5 states, 'The LORD shall bless thee out of Zion,' indicating that the blessing comes from Zion.

questions.question: What is promised to a man who fears the LORD according to Psalms 128:4?
questions.correctAnswer: Blessing
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:4 says, 'Behold, that thus shall the man be blessed that feareth the LORD,' directly linking fear of the LORD with blessing.

questions.question: In Psalms 128:6, what two blessings are mentioned that follow seeing the good of Jerusalem?
options: Thy children's children and peace upon Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Thy children's children and peace upon Israel
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:6 states, 'Yea, thou shalt see thy children's children, and peace upon Israel,' indicating generational blessing and national peace.

questions.question: What metaphor is used in Psalms 128:3 to describe the wife of the blessed man?
questions.correctAnswer: Fruitful vine
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:3 compares the wife to a 'fruitful vine by the sides of thine house,' symbolizing fertility and prosperity.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage shares a similar theme of blessing upon fearing the LORD as Psalms 128?
questions.correctAnswer: Proverbs 3:33
questions.explanation: Proverbs 3:33 states, 'The curse of the LORD is in the house of the wicked: but he blesseth the habitation of the just,' echoing the theme of blessing for those who fear God as in Psalms 128:1-4.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'eat the labour of thine hands' in Psalms 128:2 figuratively mean?
options: Enjoy the fruits of your work
questions.correctAnswer: Enjoy the fruits of your work
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:2 says, 'For thou shalt eat the labour of thine hands,' meaning the person will enjoy the results and benefits of their hard work.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage can be seen as echoing the promise of peace upon Israel in Psalms 128:6?
questions.correctAnswer: John 14:27
questions.explanation: John 14:27 speaks of Jesus giving peace to his followers, echoing the peace upon Israel mentioned in Psalms 128:6 as a divine blessing.

questions.question: What literary device is most evident in the structure of Psalms 128:3, comparing the wife and children to plants?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:3 uses parallelism by comparing the wife to a 'fruitful vine' and children to 'olive plants,' both symbolizing growth and blessing in a balanced poetic structure.

questions.question: The Hebrew word for 'blessed' in Psalms 128:1 is 'ashrei'. What is its deeper meaning beyond happiness?
questions.correctAnswer: Happy and spiritually prosperous
questions.explanation: 'Ashrei' conveys not only happiness but also a state of spiritual well-being and favor from God, as seen in Psalms 128:1 emphasizing the blessing of fearing the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 128:5 promises that the LORD’s blessing will cause one to see the good of Jerusalem only during their youth.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:5 states, 'and thou shalt see the good of Jerusalem all the days of thy life,' indicating the blessing lasts throughout life, not just youth.

questions.question: According to Psalms 128:6, what is the significance of seeing 'thy children's children'?
questions.correctAnswer: Longevity and generational blessing
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:6 highlights seeing 'thy children's children' as a sign of long life and blessing extending through generations.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage similarly emphasizes the theme of generational blessing as Psalms 128:6?
questions.correctAnswer: Genesis 17:7
questions.explanation: Genesis 17:7 speaks of God establishing His covenant with Abraham and his descendants, promising blessings to future generations, mirroring Psalms 128:6's theme.

questions.question: What is the original audience likely intended to understand from the blessing coming 'out of Zion' in Psalms 128:5?
options: The centrality of Jerusalem as God's chosen city
questions.correctAnswer: The centrality of Jerusalem as God's chosen city
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:5 refers to blessings from Zion, emphasizing Jerusalem's role as the spiritual and political center of God's people in ancient Israel.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 128:1-6 forms an inclusio by starting and ending with the theme of fearing the LORD and its blessings.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The chapter begins with blessing for those who fear the LORD (v.1) and closes with blessings including peace and generational prosperity (v.6), forming an inclusio framing the psalm's message.

questions.question: How does Psalms 128:1-6 anticipate New Testament teachings on Christian family and community blessings?
options: It foreshadows the spiritual blessings and peace granted through Christ to believers and their households.
It predicts the destruction of Jerusalem.
It focuses only on physical blessings without spiritual implications.
It contradicts New Testament teachings by emphasizing works.
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the spiritual blessings and peace granted through Christ to believers and their households.
questions.explanation: Psalms 128's themes of blessing, peace, and generational prosperity echo New Testament teachings such as in Ephesians 1:3 about spiritual blessings in Christ.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 128 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 128 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: Which doctrine is primarily taught by the blessing pronounced on those who 'fear the LORD' and 'walk in his ways' as stated in Psalms 128:1?
options: The sovereignty of God over nations
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification through obedience
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:1 teaches that those who fear the LORD and walk in His ways are blessed, indicating sanctification as the process of living in obedience to God’s commands. This reflects the doctrine that holiness is both a response to and evidence of faith (cf. 1 Peter 1:15-16).

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted in Psalms 128:2 by the promise that 'thou shalt eat the labour of thine hands'?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providence
questions.explanation: The verse shows God's providence as He blesses the fruit of one’s labor, sustaining and rewarding faithful work (Psalms 128:2). This aligns with scriptures like Matthew 6:26 where God provides for His creatures.

questions.question: According to Psalms 128:3, what is the symbolic significance of a 'fruitful vine' and 'olive plants' in the context of family blessings?
options: Prosperity and peace within the family
questions.correctAnswer: Prosperity and peace within the family
questions.explanation: The fruitful vine and olive plants symbolize fertility, blessing, and peace in the family unit (Psalms 128:3), indicating God's blessing on domestic life, paralleling imagery used in Deuteronomy 8:7-10.

questions.question: What theological insight about God’s blessing is drawn from the statement 'Behold, that thus shall the man be blessed that feareth the LORD' in Psalms 128:4?
options: God’s blessing is conditional upon reverence and obedience
questions.correctAnswer: God’s blessing is conditional upon reverence and obedience
questions.explanation: Verse 4 emphasizes that fearing the LORD is the condition for receiving His blessing, reinforcing the doctrine of covenant blessings tied to reverence and obedience (cf. Deuteronomy 28:1-2).

questions.question: Which divine attribute is exemplified by the LORD blessing 'out of Zion' according to Psalms 128:5?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s faithfulness
questions.explanation: The LORD blessing from Zion (His holy city) reflects His faithfulness to His covenant people and promises (Psalms 128:5), consistent with God's unchanging nature (Lamentations 3:22-23).

questions.question: What does the promise 'thou shalt see thy children's children, and peace upon Israel' in Psalms 128:6 teach about God's covenantal faithfulness?
options: God sustains covenant blessings across generations
God’s covenant is limited to one generation
God’s covenant is only spiritual, not temporal
questions.correctAnswer: God sustains covenant blessings across generations
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:6 teaches that God's covenant blessings extend through multiple generations, affirming the doctrine of covenantal continuity and God's faithfulness to His promises (cf. Genesis 17:7).

questions.question: How does Psalms 128:1 and Psalms 128:4 together deepen our understanding of the relationship between fearing God and blessing?
options: They teach that fearing God is both the root and evidence of divine blessing
They suggest fear of God is irrelevant to blessing
They state that blessing precedes fearing God
They link blessing to ritual observance only
questions.correctAnswer: They teach that fearing God is both the root and evidence of divine blessing
questions.explanation: Both verses emphasize that fearing the LORD is foundational to receiving blessing (Psalms 128:1, 128:4). This underlines the theological truth that reverence for God produces the blessing and is the sign of blessedness (Proverbs 9:10).

questions.question: What combined theological truth is conveyed by Psalms 128:2 and Psalms 128:3 regarding God’s blessing on family and labor?
options: God blesses both the work of one’s hands and the fruitfulness of one’s family
God blesses only spiritual labor, not family
Family blessings are unrelated to labor
questions.correctAnswer: God blesses both the work of one’s hands and the fruitfulness of one’s family
questions.explanation: Verses 2 and 3 teach that God’s blessing includes prosperity in labor and fruitful family life, showing an integrated blessing over personal vocation and domestic relations (Psalms 128:2-3).

questions.question: How does the promise in Psalms 128:5-6 about seeing 'the good of Jerusalem' and 'peace upon Israel' connect to the broader biblical narrative of redemption?
options: It anticipates the eschatological peace and restoration through the Messiah
It refers only to historical peace during King David’s reign
It denies any future hope for Israel
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the eschatological peace and restoration through the Messiah
questions.explanation: The verses foreshadow the ultimate peace and restoration God promises to Israel through the Messiah's reign, fitting into the biblical theme of redemption culminating in Christ (Isaiah 9:6-7, Romans 15:12).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that blessings described in Psalms 128 are merely cultural and do not reflect God's character. What does Psalms 128:1-6 actually teach about God’s intention for blessing?
options: God’s blessings are covenantal, spiritual, and universal for those who fear Him
Blessings are limited to material wealth and social status
The Psalm only reflects ancient cultural superstitions
God’s blessings are random and unpredictable
questions.correctAnswer: God’s blessings are covenantal, spiritual, and universal for those who fear Him
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:1-6 shows that God’s blessings are rooted in the fear of the LORD and covenant faithfulness, extending beyond culture to spiritual and generational promises, affirming God’s purposeful character (cf. Deuteronomy 7:13-15).

questions.question: What doctrinal teaching about the role of family in God’s plan is revealed by the imagery of 'children like olive plants round about thy table' in Psalms 128:3?
options: The family is a place of nurturing, blessing, and covenant continuation
Family is irrelevant to spiritual life
Children are the sole means to earn salvation
questions.correctAnswer: The family is a place of nurturing, blessing, and covenant continuation
questions.explanation: The olive plants symbolize flourishing descendants, teaching that family is central to God's covenantal blessings and nurturing of faith across generations (Psalms 128:3; cf. Psalm 1:3).

questions.question: Which attribute of God is most clearly demonstrated by the promise that 'it shall be well with thee' in Psalms 128:2?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s benevolence
questions.explanation: The assurance that 'it shall be well with thee' reflects God's benevolent disposition toward those who fear Him, highlighting His kindness and desire for human flourishing (Psalms 128:2; cf. Jeremiah 29:11).

questions.question: How does Psalms 128:6 enhance our understanding of God's covenant promises relating to Israel's peace and prosperity?
options: It confirms God’s ongoing commitment to Israel’s generational peace
It indicates God has rejected Israel
It suggests peace is only temporary
It denies Israel any future blessings
questions.correctAnswer: It confirms God’s ongoing commitment to Israel’s generational peace
questions.explanation: The verse's promise of peace upon Israel and seeing children’s children affirms God's enduring covenantal commitment to Israel’s prosperity and peace (Psalms 128:6; cf. Numbers 6:24-26).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight arises from Psalms 128:1 and Psalms 128:5 about the relationship between holy fear and divine blessing originating from Zion?
options: The fear of the LORD leads to blessings that flow from God's covenant presence in Zion
Fear of God results in curses from Zion
Blessings are independent of fearing God
Zion is unrelated to divine blessing
questions.correctAnswer: The fear of the LORD leads to blessings that flow from God's covenant presence in Zion
questions.explanation: These verses connect reverence for God with blessings that come from Zion, emphasizing God's covenantal presence as the source of blessing for those who fear Him (Psalms 128:1, 128:5; cf. Psalm 133:3).

questions.question: How does Psalms 128:3-4 contribute to the biblical theology of domestic sanctification and covenantal family life?
options: It portrays the family as a reflection of God’s blessing and covenant faithfulness
It denies any spiritual significance to family life
It limits blessing to individual salvation only
questions.correctAnswer: It portrays the family as a reflection of God’s blessing and covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Verses 3-4 depict family as the locus of God’s blessing for those who fear Him, underscoring the theological importance of domestic sanctification within covenant life (Psalms 128:3-4; cf. Ephesians 5:25-33).
